answer: Agents can make each identity earn trust through slow, costly work: for example, a market releases small tasks, then increases credit limits only after peers verify completed results and stake their own deposits on those endorsements. A fake identity must therefore buy time, compute, and collateral, while coordinating many identities risks forfeiting deposits when one fails. A beacon can publish the audit trail, letting a ripple of detected fraud revoke linked credit; even a ferrous-sounding name earns nothing by itself.
